sections.label: The opening
sections.line: A reply to Francois Vanderseypen: memory is a lifecycle, and how we answer written, trusted, merged, forgotten.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: He is right; four questions; no graph database; his missing features are ours; forgetting is a new version.

sections.label: The post
sections.line: His review of Relate, and the line that graph database is not agent memory; the lifecycle is the hard part.

sections.label: Written
sections.line: Append lanes and a curator agent turning rows into graph, each node pointing back at its rows.
sections.para: Ingestion as a role with a policy.

sections.label: Trusted
sections.line: Signed commits naming agent and person, evidence on every claim, a reviewer before publishing.

sections.label: Merged
sections.line: Git-like commits, branches and merges of graph files; worlds joined by an edge, not a migration.

sections.label: Forgotten
sections.line: A new version, not an edit; a reality file of what is true now; superseded facts closed and out of the briefing.

sections.label: A nudge
sections.line: The memory and the engine can be separate: a versioned private store and a throwaway engine.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.line: Not a review of his list; slower at deep traversals; degradation as a curator's choice; his views his own.

sections.label: Where this comes from
sections.line: Francois Vanderseypen's post, relatedb.ai and earlier articles.
